---
title: "Infer layered networks from paired RNA and ATAC"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
	eval = isTRUE(getOption("scop.grn.multiome", FALSE)))
```

## Prepare the paired PBMC input

This tutorial starts with the 500 paired PBMC cells packaged with scop. It
normalizes RNA and ATAC, prepares multiCSN candidates once, and fits B-cell and
monocyte networks through the same `RunGRN` entry point.

Install the independent [multiCSN package](https://github.com/mengxu98/multiCSN)
and a matching hg38 BSgenome before running the main example. This interface
requires multiCSN 0.1.0 or later. The selected genome must match your peak
coordinates and gene annotation. Run the chunks interactively, or set
`options(scop.grn.multiome = TRUE)` when rendering the main example.

```{r paired-input}
library(scop)
data("pbmcmultiome_sub", package = "scop")
paired <- pbmcmultiome_sub
genome <- getExportedValue("BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38", "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38")
peak_ranges <- multiCSN::parse_peak_ranges(rownames(paired[["peaks"]]))
keep <- as.character(GenomeInfoDb::seqnames(peak_ranges)) %in%
	GenomeInfoDb::standardChromosomes(genome)
paired[["peaks"]] <- subset(paired[["peaks"]], features = rownames(paired[["peaks"]])[keep])
paired <- Seurat::NormalizeData(paired, assay = "RNA",
	normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000, verbose = FALSE)
paired <- Signac::RunTFIDF(paired, assay = "peaks", verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(paired[["RNA"]]), colnames(paired[["peaks"]])))
table(paired$CellType)
```

The reference-compatible filter uses the actual matrix peak IDs. It retains
11,996 of the 12,000 packaged peaks. Both RNA and ATAC need one exact `data`
layer for multiCSN. Use `SeuratObject::JoinLayers()` first if your assays have
split layers.

Choose target genes before fitting. Here, the 64 highest-variance annotated RNA
genes define the demonstration target set. The bundled motif map supplies the
candidate TFs.

```{r paired-targets}
rna <- SeuratObject::LayerData(paired, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
variance <- Matrix::rowMeans(rna^2) - Matrix::rowMeans(rna)^2
annotated <- unique(as.character(Signac::Annotation(paired[["peaks"]])$gene_name))
variance <- variance[names(variance) %in% annotated]
targets <- names(sort(variance, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(64L)]
stopifnot(length(targets) == 64L)
```

## Fit independent network layers

```{r paired-network}
paired <- RunGRN(
	paired, methods = "multiCSN", input_mode = "multiome",
	assay = "RNA", layer = "data", atac_assay = "peaks", atac_layer = "data",
	group.by = "CellType", groups = c("B", "Mono"), targets = targets,
	resources = list(genome = genome), method_args = list(preset = "state"),
	work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pbmc-multicsn"),
	cores = 1L, seed = 1201L, verbose = FALSE
)
names(GetGRN(paired, what = "result")$groups)
GetGRN(paired, group = "B", what = "parameters")
```

`group.by` defines separate fits. Each group retains its actual cells, targets,
candidate regulators, parameters, and native results. The complete network is stored in the same Seurat object.
Choose a group when reading or plotting a group-specific network.

The `state` and `timepoint` presets supply different fitting defaults. Explicit
`method_args` override their corresponding preset values. For example,
`list(preset = "timepoint", min_detected = 5L)` uses the timepoint preset and the
requested detection threshold. Inspect `GetGRN(..., what = "parameters")` for
the effective settings used in each group.

```{r inspect-layered-network}
tf_gene <- GetGRN(paired, group = "B", layer = "tf_gene")
tf_region <- GetGRN(paired, group = "B", layer = "tf_region")
region_gene <- GetGRN(paired, group = "B", layer = "region_gene")
chains <- GetGRN(paired, group = "B", what = "chains")
native <- GetGRN(paired, group = "B", what = "native")
head(tf_region[, c("source", "target", "standardized_beta", "deletion_delta_bic",
	"raw_score", "sign", "sign_basis")])
native$summary
stopifnot(identical(tf_gene$raw_score, native$tf_gene$weight))
```

Each endpoint layer has its own regression coefficient and deletion evidence.
The standard `sign` column comes from that layer's coefficient. The native
triplet table retains path evidence and backbone-support flags. The
`mediated_tf_gene` layer retains its separate native definition.

```{r paired-network-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
GRNPlot(paired, group = "B", type = "network", layer = "tf_gene", top_n = 50L)
```

```{r paired-layered-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
GRNPlot(paired, group = "B", type = "layered", top_n = 20L)
```

```{r paired-save}
result_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc-multicsn-grn.rds")
saveRDS(paired, result_file)
reloaded <- readRDS(result_file)
stopifnot(identical(GetGRN(paired, group = "B"), GetGRN(reloaded, group = "B")))
```

Use `GetGRN(..., what = "gene_sets")` with `CellScoring` to score predicted
target programs. The [RNA tutorial](grn-framework.html#score-the-predicted-target-programs)
shows the existing `FeatureDimPlot` and `GroupHeatmap` plotting path.

## Run multiCSN independently

The standalone package remains the owner of multiCSN inference. You can use
its public API directly with the same preprocessed input and target set.
The scop adapter calls these public functions and stores their native result.

```{r standalone-multicsn, eval=FALSE}
candidates <- multiCSN::prepare_candidates(
	paired, group.by = "CellType", genome = genome,
	rna_assay = "RNA", peak_assay = "peaks", targets = targets, verbose = FALSE
)
b_network <- multiCSN::fit_layered_network(
	candidates, cell_group = "B", preset = "state", store = FALSE,
	cores = 1L, verbose = FALSE
)
multiCSN::write_network_endpoints(b_network, file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc-B-endpoints"))
stopifnot(multiCSN::validate_network_endpoints(file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc-B-endpoints")))
citation("multiCSN")
```

For an RNA-only multiCSN fit, select `input_mode = "rna"`. The independent
inferCSN implementation supplies the RNA numerical kernel. This route accepts
a gene-by-cell expression matrix and optional cell-ID-named pseudotime.

## Fit Pando interaction models

Pando uses the current R session unless multiCSN is already loaded. In that
case it runs in a separate R process to keep both packages' network methods
available. Prepare Pando and its
reference dependencies once, or provide an existing Rscript and library paths.
The following recipe uses the same normalized PBMC object and targets. The
Pando defaults retain its native module thresholds.

```{r paired-pando, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = "pando", components = "r")
pando_grn <- RunGRN(
	paired, methods = "Pando", input_mode = "multiome",
	assay = "RNA", layer = "data", atac_assay = "peaks", atac_layer = "data",
	group.by = "CellType", groups = "B", targets = targets,
	resources = list(genome = "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38"),
	return_type = "result", work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pbmc-pando"),
	cores = 1L, seed = 1201L, verbose = FALSE
)
pando_native <- GetGRN(pando_grn, group = "B", what = "native")
head(pando_native$coefficients)
head(GetGRN(pando_grn, group = "B", layer = "tf_region"))
GRNPlot(pando_grn, group = "B", type = "layered", top_n = 20L)
```

Pando's native interaction coefficients retain `estimate`, `pval`, and `padj`.
Its TF-region and region-gene projections describe membership in retained
interactions. Those projected edges have `score_type = "membership"` and
unknown sign. The native module and interaction tables remain available.

To run Pando in a separate R process, set an interpreter, a library, or a
timeout. For an existing isolated installation, set
`method_args = list(runtime = list(rscript = "/path/to/Rscript",
r_library = c("/path/to/pando-library", "/path/to/other-library")))`.

## Prepare LINGER counts and reference resources

LINGER uses paired RNA and ATAC counts, sample labels, cell-type labels, and a
matching bulk reference. Keep the bulk reference at a persistent path. The
native workflow builds pseudobulks before training and needs at least 50
pseudobulks for its SHAP sampling step. Choose a sufficiently sized input and
label design before starting training.

```{r paired-linger, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = "linger", configure_runtime = FALSE)
bulk_reference <- "/path/to/LINGER/data_bulk"
reference_tfs <- scan(file.path(bulk_reference, "TFName.txt"), what = "character", quiet = TRUE)
regulators_linger <- intersect(reference_tfs, rownames(paired[["RNA"]]))
targets_linger <- targets
linger_grn <- RunGRN(
	paired, methods = "LINGER", input_mode = "multiome",
	assay = "RNA", layer = "counts", atac_assay = "peaks", atac_layer = "counts",
	regulators = regulators_linger, targets = targets_linger,
	resources = list(bulk_reference = bulk_reference),
	method_args = list(label.by = "CellType", genome = "hg38"),
	return_type = "result", work_dir = "/path/to/new-linger-run",
	cores = 1L, seed = 1201L
)
GetGRN(linger_grn, layer = "tf_region")
GetGRN(linger_grn, what = "native")$training_coverage
```

The candidate regulators come from the reference TF list, and targets use the
prespecified RNA set. `sample.by` and `label.by` refer to existing
Seurat metadata columns. Omitting `sample.by` uses one sample. Native cell
filters retain their selected cell IDs in the result, with requested IDs and
exclusions recorded separately.

To resume an interrupted run, use a persistent `work_dir` for the first call.
Find the `linger-output` directory containing `prepare.completed.json` and
pass its path as `method_args$resume_dir` with the same inputs and settings.
LINGER verifies and copies the prepared inputs to a new run. It starts again
at preprocessing and leaves the earlier directory in place.

The three LINGER layers retain native scores and unknown sign. The result
records its LingerGRN version, training settings, and the requested seed.

## Execute the official SCENIC+ workflow

The official SCENIC+ runner starts from a prepared cisTopic model, matching GEX
AnnData, and at least two region sets. Prepare these inputs and the motif
rankings, motif scores, motif annotations, gene annotation, and chromosome sizes
for the selected genome. The cell IDs must match the selected paired input.
The prepared GEX values must also match the selected RNA layer.

The runner executes the official Snakemake workflow, including motif enrichment,
network inference, eRegulons, and AUC. Set `workflow` to the official SCENIC+
Snakemake directory when that directory is provided by a separate source
checkout. Use resource paths without whitespace or shell metacharacters.

To continue an interrupted official run, select one group and set
`method_args$resume_dir` to its existing `official` directory. Keep the
inputs, reference files, settings, and runner version the same. Snakemake
reuses finished steps and reruns incomplete ones. Keep the directory for
this scop run only. Run standalone Snakemake workflows in a separate directory.

```{r paired-scenicplus, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = "scenicplus", configure_runtime = FALSE)
scenicplus_resources <- list(
	cistopic = "/path/to/selected_cistopic_model.pkl",
	gex = "/path/to/matching_gex.h5ad",
	region_sets = "/path/to/region_sets",
	ranking_db = "/path/to/motif_rankings.feather",
	scores_db = "/path/to/motif_scores.feather",
	motif_annotation = "/path/to/motif_annotations.tbl",
	genome_annotation = "/path/to/genome_annotation.tsv",
	chromsizes = "/path/to/chromsizes.tsv",
	workflow = "/path/to/scenicplus/src/scenicplus/snakemake"
)
scenicplus_grn <- RunGRN(
	paired, methods = "SCENIC+", input_mode = "multiome",
	assay = "RNA", layer = "data", atac_assay = "peaks", atac_layer = "data",
	resources = scenicplus_resources, return_type = "result",
	work_dir = "/path/to/new-scenicplus-run", cores = 1L, seed = 1201L
)
GetGRN(scenicplus_grn, what = "native")$direct
GetGRN(scenicplus_grn, what = "native")$extended
GetGRN(scenicplus_grn, what = "native")$auc
```

`RunGRN(..., methods = "scenicplus")` is the official execution route.
The existing `RunSCENICPlus(..., backend = "python")` reads official outputs.
Its result records `execution_status = "imported"`.
The existing C++ SCENICPlus-compatible workflow has its own implementation
identity. Select the intended route explicitly when reproducing an analysis.

For each multiome method, use `GetGRN` to inspect native evidence before comparing
networks. `GRNPlot(type = "overlap", compare = ...)` compares typed edge
identities. The result retains each method's original score definition.
